title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: production traffic patterns exposed two issues in the continuous-batcher scheduler: (1) small, low-priority requests experienced starvation when high-throughput priority streams dominated the queue; (2) boundary cases with long-running KV-cache lookups caused head-of-line blocking and inflated tail latency. This PR introduces a combination of queueing and timeout strategies to improve fairness and prevent starvation while preserving aggregate throughput. Key changes: add per-priority sub-queues with age-based promotion, enforce per-request max-wait-time window with exponential backoff on retries, introduce a soft slot reservation for in-flight cold-KV lookups to avoid head-of-line blocking, and surface new metrics to observe queue depth by priority and longest-waited request. Safety: all policies are configurable via runtime flags and the default values are conservative to avoid regressions. Testing: added unit tests for fairness invariants and integration bench harnesses that reproduce previously-observed starvation patterns. Benchmarks: internal perf runs (see testing_notes) show 20-25% reduction in P95 for mixed priority workloads and no measurable throughput regression on saturated GPU pools. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to Dedicated pools, gradual ramp for hosted API with canary enabled; rollback performed by disabling the scheduler flag. Related Linear: ENG-4123, ENG-4199. Checklist: - [x] implement per-priority sub-queues and promotion policy - [x] implement max-wait-time window and timeout handling - [x] add soft reservation for KV-cold requests - [x] add observability metrics and dashboards - [x] add unit/integration tests - [x] run perf benchmarks and document results
commit_summary: tune(scheduler): add per-priority sub-queues and age-based promotion logic
feat(timeout): enforce per-request max-wait-time and exponential backoff retry path
fix(kv): add soft reservation for cold KV lookups to avoid head-of-line blocking
chore(metrics): expose queue_depth_by_priority and longest_waited_request metrics
test: add unit and integration tests that reproduce starvation cases
docs: document new scheduler flags and recommended knobs
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you explain how the age-based promotion interacts with existing batching windows? I want to ensure we won't cause extra small batches for older requests.

Asha Patel: The promotion only tags requests that exceed the promotion_threshold; we only allow promotion to preempt one batch slot per scheduling epoch, so batching windows remain largely unchanged. Added comments in scheduler.py explaining the invariant.
Priya Rao: Did you measure lock contention in the hot path after adding per-priority queues? We saw contention increases in an earlier prototype.

Asha Patel: Yes — benchmarked under 5000qps mixed workload. The implementation uses per-shard queues with lock striping; contention is within noise. Added a micro-benchmark and benchmark results in bench/perf/continuous_batcher_latency.yaml.
Kenji Yamamoto: What are the default timeout values and how can customers tune them?

Asha Patel: Defaults are conservative: max_wait_time=200ms, promotion_threshold=150ms, kv_soft_reserve_ms=30ms. All flags are documented and exposed via the runtime config. See docs/continuous-batcher.md.
Miguel Santos: Approve after CI passed and you add an observability dashboard snapshot.
ci_checks: benchmarks: pass (perf-regression-check: no regression; P95 improved for mixed workloads)
release_notes: Scheduler: improve continuous-batcher fairness and starvation prevention by adding per-priority sub-queues, age-based promotion, and max-wait-time timeouts. Introduces conservative default knobs and new observability metrics. No breaking changes.
testing_notes: Functional tests: new unit tests exercise promotion and timeout code paths. Integration: traffic replay harness against a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with mixed priority traffic (ratios 70/20/10 high/medium/low) that previously reproduced starvation. Results: baseline P95=320ms for low-priority requests, after changes P95=240ms (-25%). Aggregate throughput identical within 1-2% under saturation. Microbench: lock contention measured with perf counters showed <3% CPU time increase on scheduler hot path. Bench config and raw results saved to bench/perf/continuous_batcher_latency.yaml and archived in Linear ENG-4123.
notes_for_ops: Feature-flagged rollout. Flags: continuous_batcher.enable_fair_queues, continuous_batcher.max_wait_time_ms, continuous_batcher.promotion_threshold_ms, continuous_batcher.kv_soft_reserve_ms. Suggested canary plan: enable in one Dedicated cluster for 24h, monitor longest_waited_request and queue_depth_by_priority metrics and alert on >5% increase in overall P95 for any priority. If issues, disable continuous_batcher.enable_fair_queues to rollback.
internal_notes: We intentionally kept the promotion to a single slot preemption to avoid breaking batching density. Future work: adaptive promotion thresholds based on observed latency heatmaps and integrating with smart routing to offload long-waited requests to lower-cost model variants.
